title: On the asymptotic shape of quantile surfaces
abstract: arXiv:2609.31345v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This article is concerned with the asymptotic shape of quantile surfaces, defined as the set of quantiles at a given level $\alpha$ generated by a controlled one-dimensional distribution. Specifically, when the distribution arises as a linear combination of log-normal random variables and the control is a vector of positive coefficients, we prove that quantile surfaces are globally concave in the left tail ($\alpha\to0$) and globally convex in the right tail ($\alpha\to1$). Moreover, these surfaces exhibit asymptotic separation of scale and shape.

translated_title: 论分位数曲面的渐近形状
translated_abstract: 本文研究分位数曲面的渐近形状，其中分位数曲面定义为由受控一维分布在给定水平 $\alpha$ 下生成的分位数集合。具体而言，当该分布由对数正态随机变量的线性组合产生，且控制变量为正系数向量时，我们证明了分位数曲面在左尾（$\alpha\to0$）是全局凹的，在右尾（$\alpha\to1$）是全局凸的。此外，这些曲面还表现出尺度与形状的渐近分离特性。
tldr: 本文证明了对数正态随机变量线性组合生成的分位数曲面在左尾全局凹、右尾全局凸，并具有尺度与形状渐近分离的特性。
en_tdlr: Quantile surfaces generated by linear combinations of log-normal random variables are proven to be globally concave in the left tail and globally convex in the right tail, exhibiting asymptotic separation of scale and shape.
